title: Role of interlayer spacing and functional group on the hydrogen storage properties of graphene oxide and reduced graphene oxide
material_description: GO | Graphene oxide, brown pasty product from graphite powder below 45 um by a modified Hummers method; XRD (002) at 9.96 deg, interlayer spacing 8.84 A
functional_groups: O-H; C-O epoxy or alkoxy; C=O carboxylic acid (FTIR 3130, 1124 and 1640 cm-1)
source_location: Abstract p. 9454, 'Hydrogen storage performance' p. 9459 and Conclusion p. 9459 (uptake); pressure from the same Results sentence and the Abstract
notes: Rajaura et al. 2016, a Short Communication. NO NUMERIC MEASUREMENT TEMPERATURE EXISTS ANYWHERE FOR THIS PAPER'S OWN MEASUREMENTS. All five mentions are 'room temperature'. The paper contains two instances of '298 K' and BOTH belong to cited works by other groups, in the introduction; likewise every '77 K'. No thermostat, thermocouple, bath or cell-temperature control is described. temperature_unstated is therefore set on both rows; imputing 298 K would fabricate a condition. 80 bar is this paper's own and applies to both values: 'The rGO absorbs a small amount of molecular hydrogen 1.34 wt.% at 80 bar. However, significant increase in H2 uptake was observed in the graphene oxide at same pressure.' Distinguish it from 100 bar, which is the pressure transducer's maximum capacity, and from 1000 mbar, the hydrogen atmosphere of a separate in-situ XRD experiment. surface_area_method is none: 'BET' and 'Brunauer' return zero hits, the three 'Langmuir' hits are all the journal name in the reference list, and no nitrogen physisorption was performed at all -- characterisation is SEM, TEM, XRD, Raman and FTIR only. The 2630 cm2/gm in the introduction is a literature value for graphene in general, and the unit is itself wrong for the canonical 2630 m2/g. No pore data of any kind. Neither 'excess' nor 'absolute' occurs; the six hits of the 'absorb' family must not be matched as 'absolute'. §3.7 CONFLICTS, two, neither touching a recorded cell but both bearing on synthesis_method. The Experimental section says the reductant is hydrazine hydrate, stirred 3 h at 60 C, corroborated by the reference it cites; the XRD discussion instead says 'After the chemical reduction by hydrogen'. Separately, both the XRD and Raman discussions refer to 'chemical and thermal reduction' when no thermal reduction step exists in the Experimental section at all -- only 60 C solution stirring. Had the body text been followed, these rows would carry thermal_reduction. The Experimental section governs. The Fig. 2 caption also disagrees with the body about which panel and which colours mark the wrinkles. The conclusion hedges both values as 'about to 1.90 wt.% and 1.34wt.%' where the abstract, introduction and results state them flat; uptake_bound stays exact on the strength of the three flat statements. A third sample, pristine graphite, is extracted but NOT recorded: it has no uptake and no characterisation value any field can hold -- only an XRD interlayer spacing of 3.39 A, which is not a pore diameter. A 'hydrogenated GO' entity in Fig. 5 is likewise a post-exposure state of the graphene-oxide sample, not a separate material. Method is thin. The apparatus is home-built ('indigenous fabricated Sieverts' type volumetric setup'), designed after a cited instrument paper; the transducer's maximum is given but no make, model or accuracy. NO sample mass, NO degas duration, NO equilibration time, NO blank or helium correction and NO uncertainty are reported, despite six repeat exposures at 80 bar. Degassing is 'under rotary vacuum (1e-2 torr) at room temperature', a weak vacuum for an oxygen-functionalised carbon. The paper's own thesis -- interlayer spacing -- has no schema field. Its values: graphene oxide 8.84 A at 9.96 deg, reduced graphene oxide 3.85 A at 23.72 deg, graphite 3.39 A at 26.32 deg, hydrogenated graphene oxide 7.1 A at 12.20 deg. Note the paper reports that hydrogen exposure CONTRACTS the graphene-oxide spacing, 8.84 to 7.1 A, which sits awkwardly with its own larger-spacing-holds-more mechanism and which it attributes to strain relaxation rather than reconciling. Raman: ID/IG 0.36 rising to 0.77 on reduction, I2D/IG 0.75 implying 5-7 layers, 2D band absent in the reduced material. TIER D, on the physics override of §13.3 rather than on the additive score. 1.90 wt% at 80 bar and nominal room temperature is roughly twice the approximately 1 wt% consensus ceiling for room-temperature physisorption on pure carbons at 100 bar, and at a LOWER pressure than that bound. The paper offers a mechanism but supplies no surface area and no pore volume to support it, so the claim cannot be tested against its own data. This does not trip the validator, whose threshold is 10 wt%, which is exactly the asymmetry the tiering rubric exists to encode. Additive score: BET 0, method 1, T/P 0 (temperature never stated), uptake type 0, purity 0, calibration 0 (a volume calibration is asserted but no blank), Chahine 0 = 1. Traps: the introduction is dense with other groups' values and two are within 0.06 wt% of the reduced-graphene-oxide figure recorded here -- 1.4 wt% for graphene oxide at room temperature and 5 MPa, and 1.36 wt% for a graphene-oxide/V2O5 composite at 77 K. Nothing in the paper is close to 1.90. Also present: DOE targets of 6.0 and 9.0 wt%, theoretical predictions of 8.0, 7.5, 7.8 and about 15 wt%, and a TEM 'distance of the hexagonal lattice' of 10.35 nm that is off by about forty times from graphene's lattice constant. || C reconciliation 2026-11-09: activation_method cleared; the paper's only pre-measurement treatment is degassing ('degassed under rotary vacuum (10-2 tor) at room temperature', §2.3), which is not synthesis activation and is coded as degas_end_pressure_pa = 1.33322 Pa (10^-2 torr); degas temperature given only in words. Schema v2 fields from extractor B, checked against the paper. Fig. 8 plots hydrogen absorption (wt%) against time (s), not pressure, so it is not an isotherm and was not digitized; the value is the only one for its sample and temperature, so no isotherm_id. v0.1 row HYC-0015-M3 (pristine graphite, characterization only, no H2 uptake) dropped as outside §9 scope. Fig. 8's GO curve ends at 1.9 wt%, consistent with the printed 1.90 wt%.
